original_question: Is there an almost simple but not simple group which is recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg–Kegel graph? Note that if a group G is recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg– Kegel graph, then G is recognizable by its Gruenberg–Kegel graph, and therefore G is almost simple(P. J. Cameron, N. V. Maslova, J. Algebra, 607(2022), 186–213).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.95 in the 21st issue of The Kourovka Notebook (with notation and the definition from Problem 21.94): the existence of a finite almost simple but non-simple group recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg–Kegel graph.
correct_elements: Your draft already pinpoints the paper’s exact narrow existence question: whether there exists an almost simple but not simple group that is recognizable from the abstract isomorphism type of its Gruenberg–Kegel graph. It also correctly includes the contextual note recorded with the problem, namely that any group recognizable in this sense must be almost simple.
missing_details: The paper’s problem is about finite groups.
To be stand-alone, the Gruenberg–Kegel graph must be defined: its vertices are the prime divisors of |G|, and distinct primes p and q are adjacent if and only if G contains an element of order pq.
The phrase 'recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg–Kegel graph' must be spelled out as recognition from the underlying abstract unlabeled graph obtained by forgetting the prime labels.
The universal quantifier over comparison groups is implicit in the draft: for every finite group H, isomorphism of the unlabeled Gruenberg–Kegel graphs must force H ≅ G.
The term 'almost simple but not simple' is not unpacked; for a fully self-contained version one may specify that G has a nonabelian simple socle S with S < G ≤ Aut(S).
The Cameron–Maslova remark is contextual motivation, not part of the formal statement of the open problem.
refined_question: Does there exist a finite almost simple but non-simple group G, with nonabelian simple socle S satisfying S < G ≤ Aut(S), such that for every finite group H, if the abstract unlabeled graph obtained from the Gruenberg–Kegel graph of H by forgetting the prime labels is isomorphic to the corresponding abstract graph for G, then H ≅ G?
justification: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:1401.0300 is Problem 21.95. Its meaning depends on the immediately preceding Problem 21.94, which defines the Gruenberg–Kegel graph and the notion of recognizability by its isomorphism type via the underlying abstract graph with labels removed. Your draft is very close to the official wording, but it is not fully stand-alone because it suppresses finiteness, the unlabeled-graph interpretation, and the universal quantifier over comparison groups. The refined version restores exactly those paper-faithful details without broadening the problem.
